subject: math

entries: Pascal's triangle: the coefficients of (a + b)^n - build each row by adding the two entries above, so row 4 is 1, 4, 6, 4, 1.
slots.label: Pascal's triangle: the coefficients of (a + b)^n
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

entries: (a + b)^n, term by term - term r + 1 is C(n, r) a^(n - r) b^r: the power of a falls by one each term while the power of b rises by one.
slots.label: (a + b)^n, term by term
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

entries: Worked: expanding (2x - 3)^4 - apply the general term with b = -3 in brackets, so odd powers of (-3) are negative and the signs of the terms alternate.
slots.label: Worked: expanding (2x
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

entries: Misconception: the power does not distribute - (a + b)^2 splits into a^2, two a-by-b rectangles and b^2 in the area picture, never into a^2 + b^2 alone.
slots.label: Misconception: the power does not distribute
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

entries: The triangular array whose row n lists the coefficients of (a + b)^n; each entry is the sum of the two entries above it, and the edges are all 1.
slots.label: Pascal's triangle
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: C(n, r) = n! / (r! (n - r)!): the coefficient of the term a^(n - r) b^r in (a + b)^n, also read from row n of Pascal's triangle.
slots.label: Binomial coefficient
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: The rule (a + b)^n = the sum over r from 0 to n of C(n, r) a^(n - r) b^r, giving every term of the expansion at once.
slots.label: Binomial theorem
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: Term r + 1 of (a + b)^n, namely C(n, r) a^(n - r) b^r, used to find one chosen term - such as the coefficient of x^2 - without expanding everything.
slots.label: General term
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: The expanded sum produced by the binomial theorem, with n + 1 terms whose powers of a fall from n to 0 while the powers of b rise from 0 to n.
slots.label: Binomial expansion
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

title: A-Math binomial: Pascal's triangle and the (a+b)^n expansion
